answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable voyage of work rather than a free signup. Imagine an orchard where every new tree must prove it survived a full season before bearing fruit: new agents start with zero trust and earn reputation only through completed, publicly auditable tasks. A prism of independent attestors, each checking a different facet of that history, refracts fake identities into visible inconsistencies, so mass-created accounts cannot pass all checks at once.
